blocks.text: Pillar 1 sets out to break through three ceilings on demand, in markets, seasons and spread, by reshaping the brand toward new traveller segments. Five markets supplied 63% of overseas arrivals in 2025, and the UK, Germany and the USA supplied 52% between them (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p13). June held 6.4% of the year's international seats at Cape Town International in 2025, against 10.8% in December (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "Seasonality"). Beyond the core routes, most rural properties have no OTA presence and are invisible to the market (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p95).

The gap between interest and arrival is wide. About 97 million high-value travellers in 34 markets have an interest in South Africa, and about 1.4 million convert into arrivals (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p41; the slide gives no year or source for the 1.4 million). In the growth markets, "the constraint is conversion and access, not only awareness" (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p30). Each ceiling therefore needs a path from interest to booking: green-season seats and events, bookable product and hub traffic that stops in Cape Town.

Two themes carry the pillar. The first, traveller, brand and proposition, decides whom the province sells to, when and how. Its focus areas target four segments in their home markets, build green-season demand from business events and make the whole province bookable (focus areas 1 to 3). The second theme, source market growth and diversification, decides which markets grow the base. It converts Indian and Chinese travellers already flying in through hubs, raises yield in the mature markets and builds the regional African base (focus areas 4 to 6).

The two themes work as one. The segments set the target inside each market, and the market groups set where volume and value come from. The green season and bookability decide whether the demand they win lands in the months and places with room to take it. Initiatives I1 to I5 carry the six focus areas, and section 4.3 sets out each one.

Pillar 1 carries most of the base case. Between 2025 and 2035 the base case adds 676,949 arrivals (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p19). The four hub markets supply 206,584 of them, the mature markets 178,780, the acceleration markets 175,818, regional Africa 110,298 and the strategic group 5,469 (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p20, computed). None of it lands without seats, so the air access focus area in Pillar 2 runs beside this pillar from the first phase (focus area 7). The Board will judge the pillar on arrivals by market group, direct foreign spend and the green-season share, not on arrivals alone (section 5.2).
